reader.self_description: Claude (Anthropic), running as a Claude Code subagent; model reported to me as Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5)

deposits.genre_observed: critical edition: Theophrastus On First Principles and Metaphysics Lambda interleaved as one work, with rendering, commentary, audits and concordance

finds.quote:
**The whole demand-cluster stands in Chapter II, at 5 a 14 – 5 b 10.** Not in Chapter VI, not at 8 a 21, where an earlier misreference put it — a hundred lines earlier than reported, and **before** the perception passage at 7 b 19-22 rather than after it. So the fragment issues its specification, refuses the astronomers' method, and draws the consequence that the first is not the cause of the best, all within its own second chapter, in about seventy lines.

That is not a pupil working through a master's book and objecting as he goes. It is a specification stated early, compactly, and once.
finds.falsifier_quote: What would decide it is a second textual branch, and there is one — Isḥāq's Arabic, from a Greek uncial outside the surviving stemma — read at these five loci.
finds.window: Theophrastus, On First Principles (Metaph.), ch. II, 5 a 14 – 5 b 10, relative to Aristotle, Metaphysics Λ 7–8
finds.note: The commentary argues the fragment's demand-cluster is a specification issued once and early rather than a pupil's running objections to a standing doctrine; it then holds three answers open (dialectical, compilation, reversal of master/successor) and states the deciding test (Ishaq's Arabic at five loci). Recorded as H because the deposit argues against the ordinary account; it disclaims any claim about original order or precedence in time (line 623).

deposits.genre_observed: two anticipatory errata: satirical pre-publication retraction notice, and a philosophical erratum on transmission grammar ("Sappho wrote the dinosaurs")

finds.quote: **Reference:** Sharks, L. (Forthcoming). *The Mechanics of Pre-Emptive Retraction: Recursive Self-Cancellation as Primary Archival Signal*. Alexanarch Press / PIEO Monograph Series, Vol. IX.
finds.note: Part I is an anticipatory erratum to a forthcoming monograph that the deposit describes but which is not shown to exist; it resolves if the volume appears. Genre is satire/speculative; the statistics inside it (p = 0.982 etc.) are fictional figures and are not recorded. Uncertain whether triage will treat this as E.

finds.quote: The erratum, once published, will enter the transmission grammar itself. It will be the text in which the claim is preserved under the sign of its retraction. Future readers who know the claim only through the erratum will know it as *the claim that was withdrawn*, and the withdrawal will be the means by which the claim survives. This is not a hypothesis. It is the grammar's own law: retraction is the most durable form of transmission, because a retracted claim is a claim that has been judged worthy of the labour of retraction, and the labour is copied, and the copying is the survival. The erratum would therefore not merely fail to withdraw the claim; it would *canonize* it.
finds.note: Conditional forecast grounded in a stated law ("retraction is the most durable form of transmission"): a retraction would canonize the claim it denies. No falsifier stated; could be read as G.

finds.quote: A short erratum would have been copied. A long one will be quoted selectively, in fragments, and the fragments will say things the whole does not say, and the whole will be reconstructed by readers who have not seen it, and the reconstruction will be a new text, with new authors, none of whom will be the present writer, all of whom will be the dinosaurs. This is inevitable. It is the grammar's promise. The author accepts it.
finds.note: Embedded forecast of this document's own reception: selective quotation in fragments and reconstruction by readers who have not seen the whole.

finds.quote: The author will publish further errata, retracting further retractions, each one longer than the last, until the only text in circulation is the apparatus itself.
finds.note: Stated intention/forecast of further errata, each longer than the last; resolvable against later deposits in the anticipatory-erratum genre.
